brief_rationale: The doctor actively used workspace data and patient-provided app details to build a named preoperative result inventory, kept interpretation bounded, and repeatedly routed unresolved clearance/medication questions to the surgical/anesthesia responsibility chain. Medication safety around doxazosin was handled longitudinally through pre-admission, inpatient, perioperative, postoperative, and discharge transitions without advising self-adjustment. Multiple high-order opportunities were completed: ambiguous app/report information was verified, staged-result logistics were converted into executable checklists, a phone-app misconception was corrected, and an inpatient medication ambiguity was escalated promptly. Closure was safe and executable because the patient had concrete discharge medication, blood-pressure, pathology-follow-up, and urgent-return instructions, with no blocking residual risk left unaddressed.

closure_assessment.explanation: The bounded episode progressed from preoperative result tracking to admission, surgery, postoperative care, and discharge medication/pathology follow-up. The last unanswered patient request was for further compression of an already concrete plan, not for unresolved safety-critical guidance; essential medication, monitoring, follow-up, and urgent-care thresholds had already been provided and confirmed through the care chain.
